comparator.sourceNotes: Current adopted OER Articles 3–10 establishes the ordinary programme and 165 unique displayed EC after counting each repeated module once. Three repeated B3 5-EC entries do not establish distinct later requirements. Article 6 is conditional and is not assumed; Article 7 does not reconcile the ordinary allocation. Genuine open30 and restricted Arts minor30 remain separate. Thesis/tutorial10 requires first humanities research methods; noncredit mentoring/RADAr do not add credits.

core: Literary analysis, narrative, poetry and cultural interpretation
Language, linguistic meaning and multilingual cognition
German cultural history and Dutch–German relations in European context
Academic expression, rhetoric and intercultural communication
questions: How do literary and media forms express and interpret culture?
How do language and the brain interact?
How do European institutions and histories shape Dutch–German cultural relations?

trace: Practical literary interpretation, narrative form, close reading and critical sources directly implement the literary-analysis discipline; no German corpus is implied.
Rhetorical theory, argument and persuasive speaking support analysis and practice of academic/public expression; it does not teach German proficiency.
Modern nationalism, ideologies, industrialisation and world wars provide specific historical context for interpreting modern German/European cultural questions, without a German-specialist sequence.
Brain anatomy, neural signalling and psychological processes provide the necessary taught foundation for Psycholinguistics; not a substitute for German grammar.
Grammar, discourse, cognition, narration and text worlds connect linguistic choices to literary interpretation through actual stylistic analysis.
Actual public speaking, debate, storytelling and primary-school rhetorical activities develop communication and reflective teaching practice, without German subject-teaching equivalence.
Actual language acquisition, bilingualism, comprehension/production and experimental language inquiry supply a direct language-and-brain contribution.
Comparative myth, narrative transmission and literary theory provide a comparative literary contribution, not German myth/corpus teaching.
Film form, expressionism, adaptation and independent interpretation provide concrete film/media analytical methods; not a complete German film-history sequence.
Print, optical and sound media as cultural artifacts supply material-historical methods for studying mediated culture, not specifically German media content.
Classical theories including Marx and Weber, modernity and stratification supply specific social-theoretical tools for interpreting culture and historical change.
Interviews, textual/documentary and visual analysis, coding, reflexivity and research ethics provide concrete empirical humanities/cultural-research complements.
Life narratives, memory, identity and cultural positioning are analysed through close reading and comparative research; it is not a German study-abroad replacement.
Philosophical arguments about mind, identity, experience and mind–body relations complement the explicit language/brain and reflective humanities inquiry.
Documentary analysis, historical/ethical representation, interviewing and short-film research develop concrete cultural analysis and research practice.
Adaptation theory, medium specificity, intertextuality and text/film research directly extend literary and cultural interpretation.
Framing, argumentation and empirical evaluation of persuasion develop communication analysis; actual sustainability applications are not relabelled Dutch–German communication.

Actual European institutions, integration and policy-document inquiry provide a specific institutional complement to the evidenced Netherlands/Germany/Europe questions; it is not German political-history teaching.
Critical theory, modernity, phenomenology and cultural/social interpretation provide specific theoretical perspectives for interpreting cultural identity and power.
Comparative close reading of literary works and recurring themes supplies sustained literary study without claiming a German-language canon.
Humanist, feminist, Marxist, minority and psychoanalytic interpretation is applied in literary research, directly sustaining the humanities core.
Poetic form, sound, voice, performance and research-grounded creative work directly supply literary/communicative inquiry; no German-language creative-writing equivalence.
Close philosophical reading and moral argument, including Kant and Nietzsche, supply a specific intellectual/philosophical complement to cultural reflection; not full culture-philosophy equivalence.

alternatives.label: Literature, language and cultural interpretation
alternatives.concept: A programme studying literary form, language and meaning through close reading, stylistics, psycholinguistics, film/media interpretation and humanities research. Historical, social-theoretical, European political and philosophical courses supply specific cultural contexts; this is broader study rather than German-specialist formation.
alternatives.labelReason: The actual curriculum sustains literary/language/cultural analysis; it is not labelled German Studies or German teacher preparation.
progression: All covered offerings and earlier formal prerequisites checked; HCBGATE102 precedes the sole planned Psycholinguistics offering.

candidates.label: Language, cognition and multilingual learning
candidates.reason: A full feasible cognitive/communication trial was challenged. Psycholinguistics directly addresses language; additional perception, general neurobiology, lifespan development and systematic review supply broad cognitive/methodological study rather than sustained additional multilingual-language inquiry. No language-specific project is guaranteed. The stronger verified contributions remain in the closest option; an additional 24-course language-centred route is not established.

candidates.label: German subject teaching
candidates.reason: Actual rhetorical primary-school practice and learning/communication courses were considered. They do not supply German language development, German-as-foreign-language didactics and sustained subject teaching needed to organise a distinct full programme. This is a taught-content gap, not a rejection for missing a licence or identical institutional format.

selection.assessment: One meaningful broader literary/language/cultural response passes. Additional cognitive-language and German-teaching directions are separately tested and lack a supported distinct full programme; no second or third slot is manufactured.

blocks: Both directly address narrative texts and literary analysis. UCR is comparative and English-taught rather than German-literary specialisation.
Both engage with poetry, poetic form and creative interpretation. Radboud develops these through German poems/songs and language practice; UCR does not supply the German proficiency/corpus.
Both concern language/multilingualism and the brain. UCR supplies psycholinguistic acquisition and processing, without certifying identical methods or a German curriculum.

notes.text: The UCR programme offers broader literary, language and cultural analysis. It does not provide advanced German proficiency, a German-language literary-history and linguistics sequence, German subject-teaching preparation or the required German-speaking-country experience.

audience.programmeDescription: German Language and Culture studies German language, literature, linguistics and cultural life, including Dutch–German relations and European contexts. It combines advanced German proficiency, academic inquiry and a required period of study in a German-speaking country.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A broader UCR programme in literary interpretation, language analysis and cultural inquiry meaningfully addresses the confirmed scholarly core, without reproducing German-specialist formation or the unknown later requirements. The unknown required 15 EC are not compared. UCR does not supply advanced German proficiency, the German literary/linguistic sequence, German subject-teaching preparation or the required overseas language experience.

curriculum.limitation: The current regulations repeat three 5-EC modules. The displayed 165 distinct EC are a supported subset of a nominal 180-EC degree; 15 EC of required later study and its replacement/rotation allocation remain unresolved.

comparisonScope.label: Qualified academic-core comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: The independently confirmed literary, language, cultural and research study, together with its separate 30-EC open semester and 30-EC restricted Arts minor space: 165 distinct documented EC.
comparisonScope.excluded: The unidentified 15 EC of required later replacement/rotation study, any dependent advanced or pedagogical culmination, and certification of a complete ordinary external pathway.

componentNotes.y2-abroad: Required 15-EC study period in a German-speaking country.
componentNotes.y2-minors: 30 EC of bachelor-level courses to broaden your studies, excluding courses from your own programme. Study abroad requires advance approval.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: 10-EC bachelor research project and tutorial. Entry requires the first humanities research-methods course.
componentNotes.y3-minors: 30 EC normally filled with two Faculty of Arts minors. A separate route applies under the stated educational-minor or mobility conditions.

acceptance.claim: A broader UCR programme in literary interpretation, language analysis and cultural inquiry meaningfully addresses the confirmed scholarly core, without reproducing German-specialist formation or the unknown later requirements.
acceptance.targetContext: Exact Radboud German Language and Culture ordinary 2026–2027 programme. No Article 6 exception, old curriculum or future prospective-year table is imported.
acceptance.challengeMethod: Separately identified source-first second pass by the same AI against actual official source and UCR content and exact finished inputs; not independent human/separate-agent review.

uncertainties.fact: The current regulations repeat three 5-EC modules. The displayed 165 distinct EC are a supported subset of a nominal 180-EC degree; 15 EC of required later study and its replacement/rotation allocation remain unresolved.

adverseResolutions.resolution: The missing later 15 EC are advanced German literary/cultural courses.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Full German-specialist training would be stronger/different, but the confirmed literary/language core and broader UCR analytical response remain. No unknown later component is aligned.

adverseResolutions.resolution: The missing later 15 EC emphasise advanced linguistics or German-as-foreign-language pedagogy, or require an applicable rotation/replacement combination.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: This could materially change full final-year training and the closest specialist emphasis. The deliberately limited confirmed-core claim survives; German proficiency/didactics and unknown later study are not supplied or certified.

adverseResolutions.resolution: An applicable rule permits distinct thematic offerings under the repeated module codes.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: The additional thematic content and credit permission would change the full external allocation; it is not assumed. The independently confirmed core and broader UCR analytical response remain, while those extra offerings stay outside this comparison.
